components.boundary: HIA scanner/parser supports general ASCII module/function/SSA/formal/block identifiers and arbitrary entry declaration order in the bounded assembly profile. A separate explicitly selected HIA source lexical recognizer handles high-level Hepta token grammar, UTF-8 positions, diagnostics, arbitrary-size integer magnitudes and decimal-to-binary64 rounded bits; An explicitly selected HIA iterative type-grammar parser handles qualified/generic/ref/raw/array types, exact depth/diagnostics and generic-close split actions; Python object construction, declaration/statement/expression AST parsing and the default reference remain. Explicitly selected HIA JSON decoding/canonicalization are integrated into existing inputs. A separate HIA primitive v8 JSON Core representation frontend emits assembly for real native semantic compilation; host drivers still handle manifests, allocation, files and child receipts. Foreign-object bridging and caller-owned serialization remain Python. Explicit scalar-export JSON representation requires operator ELF selection; general module graphs, composites/full frontend grammar and whole-runtime replacement remain open.

Native fixed-profile checks exist; composite elaboration and general result signatures remain open; bounded scalar/owner/parameter-bound loan tuples are implemented and require current-source qualification.

A bounded one-shot SHA-256 algorithm is implemented in HIA and can be explicitly selected for Core content digests; host code-custody hashing remains. Core reference interpretation, general runtime/task/I/O and the complete production library remain open.

HIA writes bounded Linux x86-64 flat/ELF images, including multiple exact-name scalar C exports and allocator relocations. General module/link graphs, resource-bearing public ABI, actual shared-object linking and other native targets remain Python/external tools.
Module graphs, package locks, build orchestration and the complete frontend pipeline remain Python.
The real Agent worker/service, durable tools and protocol orchestration remain Python.
Planning/optimization/translation validation and proof construction are not rewritten; finite proof scopes do not establish whole compiler refinement.

A bounded Linux stdin/stdout compiler ET_EXEC entry is authored in HIA and requires current-source qualification; production CLI, installation/materialization/release tools and whole clean-machine toolchain remain open.

metadata.evidence_kind: static inventory and explicit implementation boundary, not execution evidence

historical or adjacent-branch CI does not qualify changed source bytes
